name: lora-2b
recorded: 2026-10-12, before any LoRA-2B smoke, memory row, trajectory or score exists anywhere: no LoRA-2B run has been made on any stack and no result of one has been read. The only reads behind this record are the rulings and decisions named in design_by, the safetensors headers of the two downloaded base snapshots (dtype names and shapes, no tensor data; AUDIT/lora-2b-2026-10-09/downloads.md) and the pinned init files' digests. Written from Fable's D6 table; amendments made after any LoRA-2B result is read are void (see amendments).
status: quick, Mac only, report-only for promotion. Every Mac row of this family is quick (one seed, truncated schedule; rule 8) and cannot promote anything. A promotion-grade LoRA-2B campaign is a box campaign with its own pre-registration (3 seeds on the full schedule plus controls); nothing here registers it.
design_by: AUDIT/lora-2b-2026-10-09/fable-ft-decisions.md D1-D8 (Fable, 2026-10-09; D6 is the table below); AUDIT/lora-2b-2026-10-09/human-decisions.md (the human, 2026-10-09: approved the table, D2 head, D4 base and downloads, D8 GPU plan); AUDIT/board-sweep-2026-10-12/fable-board-sweep-ruling.md rulings 2a (stored-F32 tensors), 2g (span-head source) and 2h (this file, the optimizer_recipe labels).

words.not_comparable: LoRA-2B rows are not comparable to v5 rows (or to v0.1/v6 full-fine-tune rows) and are never pooled with them. Every knob below differs from v5's recipe, so no row-for-row reading exists. The comparison is gate verdicts and val metrics on identical sets (the same gates, thresholds, held-out and val sets as v5; rule 2: nothing here moves a threshold, a seed count or a held-out set).
words.quick: A Mac row is quick (one seed, truncated schedule) and cannot promote.
words.letter_ce: The full-vocabulary letter cross entropy at the answer positions is logged on every LoRA-2B row, report-only, with no gradient. It exists so the v0.1 'letter floor' number is available; it gates nothing.
words.claim_the_mac_row_may_make: a Rust trainer in ojas over canonical tessl kernels trained a Lappi LoRA checkpoint on the M5 Pro; the campaign's scorer scored it at X; row <id>, quick=True. Nothing stronger.

family.optimizer_recipe_note: A new value in tools/real_ft_run.py OPTIMIZER_RECIPES, so precaution 5's filter never pools a LoRA row with 'master'. The Metal full-fine-tune path's AdamW over f32 parameters is labelled 'f32' (ruling 2h) and is a different family from this one.
family.ledger_pooling: A ledger reader that pools by optimizer_recipe must not pool 'lora' with 'master', 'bf16', 'kahan' or 'f32'.

base.precision: D3: frozen base resident in bf16, GEMM operands bf16 with f32 accumulation, f32 residual stream, f32 LoRA/head/norm parameters and optimizer state. No 8-bit or 4-bit (gated on Fable's D3 measurement; not built here).

stored_f32_tensors.rule: The 36 tensors the checkpoint stores as F32 (layers.<i>.linear_attn.A_log and layers.<i>.linear_attn.norm.weight in each of the 18 GDN layers) stay f32-resident in the frozen base (ruling 2a). The torch reference arm loads with load_text_tower(..., keep_stored_dtype=<those 36 names>); the default load (v5/v6) casts them to bf16 and is unchanged.
stored_f32_tensors.dtype_map_formula: sha256 over '\n'.join(f'{name}\t{dtype}' for name in sorted(text tensor names)), the 'model.language_model.' prefix stripped, dtype as the safetensors header spells it (F32, BF16)
stored_f32_tensors.f32_names_formula: sha256 over '\n'.join(sorted names stored F32), same prefix stripped

data.shape: v5's: the v5r shard set read by Lappi's shard reader unchanged, width-bucketed rows up to 9,638 tokens, --batch-order seed. Seq 2048 and an 8x4 sequence batch are refused as the training width and batch.
data.source_of_pins: campaign/v5-preregistered.json amendments_pending (filled 2026-10-03). A LoRA-2B row whose train shard hash differs from the one above is not a LoRA-2B-registered row.
data.held_out: Held-out data and the two task-holdout families are never read by a training process (rule 3); the held-out set is read by the scorer only, as for v5.
data.gates: The gates, thresholds, val set and held-out set are v5's, unchanged (rule 2). This file defines no new gate.

width.fallback: If a measured step at T=9,638, micro-batch 1, gradient checkpointing on, does not fit the Metal working set: cap the bucket at 8,192 and drop (not truncate) every row above it, record the dropped-row count in the row, and read the needle gate as is. This is the only width change permitted, and only on that measurement.
width.memory_row: The T=9,638 memory row is measured before the Mac run (peak device bytes, ledger row, quick).

batch.note: The corpus plan is drawn at the run seed, as v5's was (corpus.plan_seed). One step is one batch, so the accumulation-weighting question (audit G7/B5) does not arise for the run; a smoke that uses grad_accum > 1 must weight by valid share.

loss.reduction: mean over the supervised positions of the batch
loss.choice: 17-way cross entropy over the 17 answer rows, f32, from the f32 residual stream (D2)
loss.span: the span pointer head's loss as in v5 (weight 1.0)
loss.report_only: full-vocabulary letter CE at the same positions, no gradient

lora.adapted_linears_count_rule: 24 MLPs x 3 + 6 attention layers x 4 + 18 GDN layers x 3
lora.frozen: every parameter outside the adapters, D17 and the span head (embedding, norms, the 36 stored-F32 tensors, conv, dt_bias, in_proj_a/b)
lora.ablation: One r=64 arm if budget allows; it is a separate row with its own label, and not registered as a gate.
lora.reference: python/qd_train/lora.py (plain torch; no peft, bitsandbytes or unsloth)

head.readout: Lappi's 17-row readout kept: up to 16 letters plus noul, softmax over those rows of the tied embedding. No Clef head for this model.
head.d17: A trainable f32 delta D17 [17, H] over the frozen embedding's answer rows, init 0; served as embed[answer ids] + D17.
head.span_head: SpanPointerHead as v5's, host f32, init pinned below

optimizer.weight_decay_scope: every trainable tensor (no bias or norm trains)
optimizer.lr_scale_form: one schedule at peak 2e-4; D17 and the span head run at lr_scale 0.5 (1e-4 at the peak, same warmup and cosine)
optimizer.layerwise_split: None. v5's 0.1x lower-layer split is dropped for LoRA. RSI-Jev's recorded prior (python/qd_train/optim.py: 'freezing those layers instead costs decision accuracy') is a prior against a frozen base; the shuffled-label control and the gates are what test it.
optimizer.implementation_note: Reference arm: qd_train.optim.build_optimizer(ADAMW_FP32) over fp32 leaves is torch.optim.AdamW (MasterWeightAdamW refuses an all-fp32 list by design), driven by apply_lr over the groups; both are unchanged.

schedule.shape: linear warmup (step+1)/warmup then cosine to min_lr 0
schedule.not: not warmup 10, not HF's step/W form

steps.full_recipe: 1 epoch (v5's 12,176 steps per seed). Registered as the full recipe; no Mac row runs it.
steps.mac: a truncated schedule of about 200 to 400 steps inside the approved 3-6 h window; quick.

h1024.what: the seed-0 init at the 0.8B smoke model's hidden size, built by the same generator
h1024.generated_with: python 3.14.7, torch 2.12.1, safetensors 0.8.0, cpu; the content digest is the one that binds, the file sha256 depends on the safetensors writer

d17.formula: run_control.TensorRef.digest of a float32 zero tensor of that shape

lora_a.rule: kaiming_uniform_(a=sqrt(5)) on each [r, in] A (so U(+-1/sqrt(in))), drawn from one CPU torch.Generator seeded with the run seed, visiting the adapted modules in model.named_modules() order (qd_train.lora.attach_lora). B = 0.
lora_a.pinned_as: a rule: the A digest is not fixed here, because it is a function of the run seed. The value is recorded in the row and checked against this rule by recomputing it with attach_lora at that seed; a mismatch voids the row.
lora_a.shapes: [16, in_features] per adapted linear, in_features read from the snapshot

smoke.warmup: max(1, steps // 20), as the recipe (Unsloth's warmup 10 is not used)
smoke.objectives: The smoke runs both objectives (17-way over the answer rows vs the full-vocabulary letter CE) on the same seed and batch order.
smoke.switch_rule: If the full-vocabulary objective beats the 17-way objective on val_top1.choice by more than 2 points AND gives a lower in-distribution abstention count, this pre-registration names the full-vocabulary objective instead for the 2B reduced run. The rule is written here, before the smoke exists; it is a decision between two registered arms and not a gate.

bounds.source: Fable D7, written before any run
bounds.a_prime: op level, CPU f32, tiny fixture (batch >= 2, >= 2 GDN heads, vocab > 8192, -100 labels): LoRA forward loss <= 1e-5 relative; dX, dA, dB within 1e-5 of each tensor's max; no dW allocated; frozen leaves' gradients absent, not zero. The reference arm's own tests (python/tests/test_lora_reference.py) hold the Python side of this.
bounds.b_prime: 20-step tiny trajectory, torch fp32 CPU vs ojas CPU Exact: per-step loss <= 1e-5 relative (steps 0-5), <= 1e-4 (to 20); final A, B, D17 within 1e-5 of each tensor's max; two ojas runs bit-identical; Metal vs CPU <= 2^-8 on loss with bf16 operands.
bounds.c_prime: real 2B Tape vs provider at T=128, and Tape-with-LoRA at B=0 loss bit-equal to Tape-without-LoRA on CPU.
bounds.d_prime: 0.8B 60-step smoke and the 2B reduced run vs torch MPS bf16 autocast, same seed, init digests and batch order: |delta loss| <= 0.02 nats steps 1-50, EMA(0.9) <= 0.05 after; the fp32 torch arm on CPU for the 0.8B smoke is the tight pin (report-only at 2B). If the torch arm cannot run the 2B at T=9,638 on MPS, d' is applied to the 0.8B smoke only and the 2B row says 'no reference arm at this shape' in its quick reason.
bounds.not_run: b', c' and d' need the ojas Tape StepProvider and the heavy slot; this record registers them and does not run them.

mac_rows.rule: Every Mac row below is quick and cannot promote. A row that is not quick is not a Mac row.

rows.what: the real-2B Tape run on the local Qwen3.5-2B instruct weights (D1's gate), about 1 h
peak device bytes at T=2,048 and T=9,638, micro-batch 1, checkpointing on, about 1 h
the 0.8B-Base 60-step smoke with its torch arm, about 2 h
the reduced 2B-Base run, a truncated schedule inside the approved 3-6 h window

mac_rows.quick_reason: one seed; a truncated schedule; neither is a full recipe (rule 8)
mac_rows.no_full_mac_campaign: A full-schedule 3-seed Mac campaign (about 500-600 GPU-hours) is not requested and not registered.

release_and_averaging.release: A merged dense bf16 tower (W' = W + (alpha/r) B A in f32, rounded once to bf16, RNE), D17 and span_head.safetensors (f32), through ckpt_average to qd-export to qd-metal. Adapters (with D17 and the span head) are the checkpoint and resume unit and are not served.
release_and_averaging.average: A seed average of LoRA-2B averages merged weights only (tools/ckpt_average.py --from lora-merged); averaging A and B separately is refused with a typed error, because mean(B)mean(A) differs from mean(BA). average_may_promote stays false (docs/promotion-decisions.json).
release_and_averaging.span_head: Whichever average is ever taken, its span head is declared by the averaging command: either --span-head-seed N (the head of the input whose checkpoint body says seed == N) or the averaged head, recorded in the manifest as span_head_source {mode, seed, input, payload_digest}. Every LoRA-2B seed starts from the same pinned span-head init above. The choice for a promotion-grade average is made in that campaign's own pre-registration before the average is scored; no Mac row averages (one seed).

ledger.label: recipe.optimizer_recipe = 'lora'
ledger.kind: every Mac row quick=true with a quick_reason naming the one seed and the truncated schedule
ledger.numbers: A number in a report cites a ledger row id (rule 5); a suite that could not run is reported as not run.

not_decided_here: The Tape StepProvider, the ojas-train move and the b'/c'/d' runs (ojas side).
D17 in qd-export and qd-metal (wave 2, lane 2b).
Any 8-bit or 4-bit format (Fable D3: gated on the mlx measurement and a demonstrated memory need).
The 4B base (a box, not this track).
The peft round-trip export test (needs the human to install peft; not asked).
amendments_rule: An amendment made after any LoRA-2B result has been read is void. A change before that is a commit that says what changed and why, and leaves the original text in the history.
